heading.en: Where does a city's waste water go?

hook.en: Bengaluru produces well over a billion litres of sewage every day. Before it reaches a lake or river, bacteria in a treatment plant eat most of the dirt for us.
hook.kn: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ನೂರು ಕೋಟಿ ಲೀಟರ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕೊಳಚೆ ನೀರು ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ಕೆರೆ ಅಥವಾ ನದಿ ಸೇರುವ ಮೊದಲು ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಾ ಘಟಕದ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಕೊಳೆಯನ್ನು ತಿಂದುಹಾಕುತ್ತವೆ.

objectives.en: Describe primary and secondary treatment of sewage
Define BOD and explain what it tells us
Explain flocs, activated sludge and anaerobic sludge digesters

narration.en: Bengaluru produces well over a billion litres of sewage every day. Before it reaches a lake or river, bacteria in a treatment plant eat most of the dirt for us.
narration.kn: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ನೂರು ಕೋಟಿ ಲೀಟರ್‌ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಕೊಳಚೆ ನೀರು ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಅದು ಕೆರೆ ಅಥವಾ ನದಿ ಸೇರುವ ಮೊದಲು ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣಾ ಘಟಕದ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಕೊಳೆಯನ್ನು ತಿಂದುಹಾಕುತ್ತವೆ.

body.en: Sewage (municipal waste water) contains large amounts of organic matter and microbes, many of them pathogenic. In sewage treatment plants (STPs) it is first given primary treatment: physical removal of particles, large and small, by sequential filtration and sedimentation. Floating debris is removed by filtration; grit (soil and small pebbles) by sedimentation. The solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant is the effluent, which goes on to secondary treatment.

points.en: Supernatant: effluent, sent to secondary treatment

narration.en: Primary treatment is purely physical: filtration removes floating debris and sedimentation removes grit. What settles is primary sludge, and the liquid on top, the effluent, goes for secondary treatment.
narration.kn: ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣೆ ಕೇವಲ ಭೌತಿಕ: ಸೋಸುವಿಕೆ ತೇಲುವ ಕಸವನ್ನು, ತಳಸೇರುವಿಕೆ ಮಣ್ಣು-ಕಲ್ಲನ್ನು ತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ತಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಉಳಿದದ್ದು ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ರಾಡಿ; ಮೇಲಿನ ದ್ರವ (ಎಫ್ಲುಯೆಂಟ್) ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣೆಗೆ ಹೋಗುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Sewage passes through two stages of treatment before the clean effluent can go into a river.
Primary treatment is physical: sequential filtration and sedimentation. The settled solids form the primary sludge.
Secondary treatment is biological. In the aeration tank, flocs of bacteria and fungal filaments eat the organic matter, so the BOD falls sharply.
BOD, the biochemical oxygen demand, is the oxygen microbes would use to oxidise all the organic matter in one litre of water. The higher the BOD, the more polluted the water.

narration.en: Sewage passes through two stages of treatment before the clean effluent can go into a river. Primary treatment is physical: sequential filtration and sedimentation. The settled solids form the primary sludge. Secondary treatment is biological. In the aeration tank, flocs of bacteria and fungal filaments eat the organic matter, so the BOD falls sharply. BOD, the biochemical oxygen demand, is the oxygen microbes would use to oxidise all the organic matter in one litre of water. The higher the BOD, the more polluted the water.

body.en: The primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated and air is pumped in. Useful aerobic microbes grow vigorously into flocs: masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments that form mesh-like structures. While growing they consume most of the organic matter, which sharply reduces the BOD. BOD (biochemical oxygen demand) is the amount of oxygen that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one litre of water were oxidised by bacteria; the higher the BOD, the greater the polluting potential. When the BOD has fallen enough, the effluent goes to a settling tank where the flocs sediment as activated sludge. A small part of it is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum; the major part goes to anaerobic sludge digesters, where anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and fungi and produce a mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide and CO$_2$ (biogas). The treated effluent is released into rivers and streams. The Ministry of Environment and Forests started the Ganga Action Plan and the Yamuna Action Plan to build more STPs.

points.en: Aeration tank: flocs (bacteria + fungal filaments) eat organic matter
BOD = O2 needed to oxidise organic matter in 1 L of water
Settling tank: activated sludge; part returned as inoculum
Anaerobic sludge digester: biogas (CH4, H2S, CO2)

narration.en: In secondary treatment, air is bubbled through the effluent and flocs of bacteria and fungal filaments eat the organic matter, lowering the BOD. The flocs settle as activated sludge; a little is reused as inoculum and the rest is digested anaerobically to give biogas.
narration.kn: ದ್ವಿತೀಯ ಸಂಸ್ಕರಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಗಾಳಿ ಹಾಯಿಸಿದಾಗ ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾ ಮತ್ತು ಶಿಲೀಂಧ್ರ ತಂತುಗಳ ಫ್ಲಾಕ್‌ಗಳು ಸಾವಯವ ವಸ್ತುವನ್ನು ತಿಂದು BOD ತಗ್ಗಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಫ್ಲಾಕ್‌ಗಳು ಸಕ್ರಿಯ ರಾಡಿಯಾಗಿ ತಳಸೇರುತ್ತವೆ; ಸ್ವಲ್ಪವನ್ನು ಮತ್ತೆ ಬಳಸಿ, ಉಳಿದದ್ದನ್ನು ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕರಹಿತವಾಗಿ ಜೀರ್ಣಿಸಿ ಜೈವಿಕ ಅನಿಲ ಪಡೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ.

problem.en: Water samples A, B and C have BOD values of 2 mg/L, 18 mg/L and 300 mg/L. Which is untreated sewage, which is clean river water, and which is moderately polluted?

steps.en: BOD measures how much oxygen bacteria would use to oxidise the organic matter in one litre.
More organic matter means more oxygen demand, so a higher BOD means more pollution.

answer.en: C (300 mg/L) is untreated sewage, A (2 mg/L) is clean water, and B is moderately polluted.
